key_insight: Long-tail fine-tune fleets keep >=1 warm replica per model; pooling them onto shared GPUs with fast loading frees much pinned HBM, mainly for multi-tenant model hosts.
killer_doubt: Prior art already ships it. 'Under 1 s' load holds only to ~13B: 70 GB FP8 at ~55 GB/s PCIe5 x16 takes ~1.3 s even before NVMe striping limits.
decisive_experiment: None needed for novelty. For the forecast: replay a public multi-model trace (Azure LLM, BurstGPT) through ServerlessLLM-style pooling and report GB-HBM-hours per model at a fixed p99 TTFT SLO.
prior_art: ServerlessLLM (OSDI'24), AlpaServe, S-LoRA/Punica multi-adapter serving, Alibaba Aegaeon (SOSP'25) token-level multi-model GPU pooling.

key_insight: Fixed-rate lossy coding gives a guaranteed 4x with none of the page fragmentation that hurt lossless capacity compression. A CXL expander serving 'lossy fp64' NUMA pages eases adoption.
killer_doubt: A 64 B writeback read-modify-writes a 4^3 block (512 B to 128 B), re-quantizing 56 untouched values. Drift over 1e4 timesteps may break bounds, and the controller needs array shape.
decisive_experiment: Run LULESH, an AMReX hydro code and HPCG for 1e4 steps on a userfaultfd page emulator (ZFP rate 8-24, RMW buffer); compare drift against full precision. Then an Agilex CXL Type-3 FPGA prototype for latency. ~$400k.
prior_art: zfp compressed arrays (LLNL), FPGA ZFP codecs (DE-ZFP), lossy-truncation memory-controller patents; no inline ZFP capacity controller found (via search snippet).

key_insight: Same core mechanism as I-09037, with the codec in the L2 fill/evict path. It also saves on-chip fabric bandwidth and is worth carrying as a variant inside the I-09037 dossier.
killer_doubt: Duplicate. An L2-side codec needs a CPU vendor to change the core uncore, while a CXL device does not. 4^3 blocks also need array strides that physical-line caches never see.
decisive_experiment: Folded into I-09037. Add one cache-simulator arm (gem5 or ZFP cached arrays at an L2-sized cache) to measure the extra bandwidth saved over the controller-side placement.
prior_art: zfp cached compressed arrays (software cache, same fill/evict semantics), FPGA ZFP codecs; hardware L2 ZFP not found.

key_insight: Frozen weights need no refresh or capacitor, and via-programmed ROM runs in mature U.S. logic fabs with one custom mask: a real capital and sourcing lever for small models.
killer_doubt: Density. 28 nm via-ROM is ~0.01-0.03 Gb/mm2 against DRAM 1b's ~0.35, so 70 GB FP8 needs ~47,000 mm2 (~0.7 wafer, ~$20/GB). Not cheaper and cannot be co-packaged.
decisive_experiment: Desk study first: price a ROM compiler macro at 28/22 nm (bits/mm2, 1-2 bit/cell) for 8B and 70B models against HBF/NAND and LPDDR $/GB and GB/s. A die only follows if ROM beats NAND.
prior_art: Taalas hard-wired model chips (8B-class, per press); SanDisk/SK hynix High Bandwidth Flash for read-only weights at ~50x DRAM density.

key_insight: Same mechanism as I-01226. Multi-bit, stacked via-ROM chiplets are the right fix for density, and offloading weights to non-DRAM would leave HBM for KV cache.
killer_doubt: Even at 2 b/cell and 8-high stacks, 70 GB needs ~2,900 mm2 of footprint against ~240 mm2 for two HBM4 stacks. NAND-based HBF does the same job ~50x denser.
decisive_experiment: Folded into I-01226's desk study. Add a stacked-ROM arm (2 b/cell, 8 dies, hybrid bond) and compare GB per package footprint and $/GB against HBF and HBM3E.
prior_art: Taalas hard-wired model silicon (per press), High Bandwidth Flash (SanDisk/SK hynix MoU 2025), multi-level implant/via ROM in MCUs.

key_insight: Outside three hyperscalers, nobody has published memory contents by workload. An on-host-aggregated atlas would calibrate the S-score of every compression, dedup and tiering idea in this study for under $1M.
killer_doubt: It saves nothing by itself. It needs >=1,000 non-hyperscale hosts across >=10 workload classes, and raw page hashes enable confirmation attacks, so only on-host aggregates may leave the host.
decisive_experiment: Ship an eBPF/DAMON agent with on-host zero/dup/entropy/coldness histograms (no hashes leave the host) to 3 partner fleets (university HPC, a mid-size SaaS, a CDN) for 90 days, then publish v0.1. ~$300k.
prior_art: Google far memory (ASPLOS'19), Meta TMO (ASPLOS'22), Microsoft Pond (ASPLOS'23) publish single-fleet statistics; no open cross-fleet atlas found.

key_insight: Treating avoided DRAM as a 'negabyte' supply lever is the right accounting frame, and federal procurement disclosure of bytes per transaction is cheap and executable without Congress.
killer_doubt: At $20/GB DRAM (~$4/GB-year amortized), the market already pays far more than a plausible credit. Counterfactual baselines invite gaming like the FERC demand-response cases, plus Jevons rebound.
decisive_experiment: Model a $0.5-1/GB-year credit against the 4x price signal using public capex data. Pilot only the procurement-disclosure half with one agency (GSA) for software buys.
prior_art: Energy-efficiency analogues: EU white certificates, 179D deduction, utility demand-response baselines; no memory-specific credit found.

key_insight: Routing easy queries to small models does cut giant-model replicas, and its HBM, roughly by the share of traffic that stays small.
killer_doubt: Already done and shipping. Escalated queries pay both models, and verifier misroutes of ~10-20% erode the claimed 3x HBM cut.
decisive_experiment: None needed for novelty. For the demand forecast: measure the routed share and HBM-hours on a public router benchmark (RouteLLM eval) at iso-quality.
prior_art: FrugalGPT (2023), RouteLLM (2024), Hybrid LLM; production routers such as OpenAI's GPT-5 fast/thinking router.

key_insight: Textures dominate game and VR memory, and neural texture compression gives a 4-8x VRAM cut over BCn when decoded at sample time.
killer_doubt: VRAM is saved only with decode-at-sample. GPUs lacking matrix cores (consoles, mobile, VR) transcode to BCn on load instead, saving disk, not DRAM. NVIDIA ships the SDK.
decisive_experiment: None for novelty. For the forecast: measure frame-time cost and VRAM cut of NTC decode-at-sample on 3 GPU tiers in one Unreal scene.
prior_art: NVIDIA RTX Neural Texture Compression SDK and SIGGRAPH'23 random-access neural texture paper; AMD neural block compression research.

key_insight: Decode leaves ~90% of tensor-core FLOPs idle, so online fitting of a compressed KV representation is nearly free in compute. The unknown is whether a field beats quantization in rate-distortion.
killer_doubt: Post-RoPE keys and values are token-content signals, not smooth in position. 20-50x needs ~0.3-0.8 bits per element, against KIVI-class 2-bit (8x) that already loses accuracy on retrieval.
decisive_experiment: Fit SIREN fields per layer and head to Llama-3-8B KV at 32k tokens with an exact recent window plus outliers. Compare against KIVI and low-rank at equal bits on RULER and needle tests. ~$30k of GPU time.
prior_art: KIVI/KVQuant quantization, Palu/xKV low-rank, H2O/SnapKV eviction; trained-in neural memory (Titans, TTT layers) is the architectural workaround.

key_insight: In batch inference the weight pass is a sequential read-only scan, so its storage medium need not be DRAM. That much is right.
killer_doubt: At 60 m/s and 0.3 um voxels a track gives ~0.6 Gb/s, so 1.25 TB/s needs >10,000 heads each servoing <100 nm. Medium cost is moot: 70 GB NAND ~$5.
decisive_experiment: Paper link budget: tracking tolerance, optical SNR and pJ/bit for a 100-head array against ~100 Gen5 SSDs or one HBF stack delivering 1.25 TB/s. Build nothing unless the head array costs less than SSDs.
prior_art: Microsoft Project Silica (archival glass, slow read); SSD/HBF weight streaming (High Bandwidth Flash, GPUDirect Storage) does the job better.

key_insight: For SRAM-only accelerators or DP-replicated small-TP serving, one central weight copy broadcast per step could free 30-60% of per-GPU HBM for KV. Cerebras already shows a weight-streaming fabric works.
killer_doubt: Tensor/expert parallelism already gives 1/N weight residency, moving ~0.7 GB/step of activations against 70 GB/step broadcast (~100x less). One 70B layer (~0.9 GB) also exceeds on-chip SRAM (~50-130 MB).
decisive_experiment: On an 8xH100 node, use NVLink SHARP multicast to stream layer shards per decode step from one GPU, and compare tok/s/GB-HBM against TP=8 at equal p99 latency. ~$50k cloud.
prior_art: Cerebras MemoryX/SwarmX weight streaming with broadcast to replicas; Megatron tensor parallelism and DeepSeek large-EP serving minimise weight replication.
